text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The editorial says a meeting of Democratic party leaders showed former president Sali Berisha may still impose himself as a political force.
- Special police forces cracked down on organised crime in the southern port town of Vlore to stop gangsters from spreading terror among the population.
- Italian general Luciano Forlani, commander of the multinational protection force troops in Albania, left the country with the last group of Italian soldiers.
- Interior ministry has started to re-organise police in the southern towns of Gjirokaster, Tepelene and Sarande.
- Cigarette smuggling is booming in the south.
- An International Monetary Fund delegation will visit Albania on August 19.

- Police intervened on Sunday to avoid clashes among soccer fans after a match of Flamurtari from Vlore against a team from Tirana, which was abandoned by the Vlore club claiming it was not granted a penalty.
- The national council of the Democratic party excluded former leader Tritan Shehu and ex-prime minister Aleksander Meksi from the party chairmanship.
- Fatos Nano, Socialist party leader and prime minister, said his leftist party should remain a strong political force.
